steps: Hands just wider than your shoulders, body in one straight line from head to heels, core and glutes tight.
Lower your chest toward the floor with elbows about 45 degrees from your body, not flared out.
Press the floor away until your arms are straight, keeping your hips level the whole way.
Push-Up.mistake: Letting the hips sag or pike up, so the chest and core stop doing the work.

steps: Hands on a bench or sturdy surface, a little wider than your shoulders, body in a straight line.
Lower your chest to the edge with elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Press back up until your arms are straight without letting the hips drop.
Incline Push-Up.mistake: Setting the hands too high and cutting the range short, so the chest never gets a full stretch.

steps: Feet on a bench, hands on the floor just wider than your shoulders, body in a straight line.
Lower your chest toward the floor with elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Press up and slightly back toward your feet until your arms lock out, keeping your core tight.
Decline Push-Up.mistake: Dropping the head forward and piking the hips, which turns the move into a shoulder press.

steps: Hands under your chest with thumbs and index fingers touching to make a diamond, body in a straight line.
Lower your chest toward your hands while keeping your elbows close to your ribs.
Press up until your arms are straight, squeezing your triceps at the top.
Diamond Push-Up.mistake: Letting the elbows flare wide, which takes the work off the triceps and strains the wrists.

steps: From a downward-dog shape with hips high, hands shoulder-width apart and legs nearly straight.
Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head toward the floor between your hands.
Press back up through your shoulders to the starting shape.
Pike Push-Up.mistake: Walking the feet in so far that the move becomes a regular push-up with no shoulder load.

steps: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out, chest tall.
Sit your hips back and down until your thighs are at least parallel, knees tracking over your toes.
Drive through your whole foot to stand up, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Bodyweight Squat.mistake: Letting the knees cave inward or the heels lift as you come out of the bottom.

steps: Start in a squat stance, chest tall, arms ready to swing.
Sit back into a quarter to half squat, then explode straight up off the floor.
Land softly on the middle of your feet, bend your knees to absorb it and go straight into the next rep.
Jump Squat.mistake: Landing stiff-legged or with the knees caving in, which sends the impact into the joints.

steps: Lean your back flat against a wall and walk your feet out until your knees are over your ankles.
Slide down until your thighs are parallel to the floor, with your lower back and shoulders against the wall.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, with your weight through your heels.
Wall Sit.mistake: Resting your hands on your thighs, which takes load off the legs, or sitting too high to feel it.

steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your hips.
Step forward and lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees, with your front knee over your ankle.
Push through the front foot to return to standing, then switch legs.
Bodyweight Lunge.mistake: Taking too short a step so the front knee travels far past the toes and the heel lifts.

steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your chest up.
Step one foot back and lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees, front shin close to vertical.
Push through the front heel to stand up, then switch legs.
Reverse Lunge.mistake: Leaning the torso forward and shifting weight onto the back foot instead of the front leg.

steps: Stand about a step and a half in front of a bench and rest the top of one back foot on it.
Lower straight down until your front thigh is parallel to the floor, torso upright, front heel planted.
Drive through the front foot to stand, then finish all reps before switching legs.
Bulgarian Split Squat.mistake: Standing too close to the bench so the front knee shoves forward and the back foot does the work.

steps: Stand facing a sturdy box or bench, with one whole foot on top.
Press through that foot to stand up fully, without pushing off the floor foot.
Lower back down slowly under control, then repeat before switching legs.
Step-Up.mistake: Using the trailing leg to spring up, so the working leg does only part of the lift.

steps: Stand tall with the balls of your feet on the floor or a step, hands on a wall for balance if needed.
Rise as high as you can onto your toes and pause for a second at the top.
Lower slowly until your heels are at or just below the step, then repeat.
Calf Raise.mistake: Bouncing through the reps with a short range instead of pausing at the top and bottom.

steps: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip just wider than your shoulders, shoulders pulled down away from your ears.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down and back.
Lower under control until your arms are fully straight before the next rep.
Pull-Up.mistake: Swinging or kipping and cutting the bottom short, so the back never gets the full range.

steps: Hang from the bar with an underhand grip about shoulder-width apart, shoulders set down.
Pull until your chin clears the bar, leading with your chest and keeping your elbows close.
Lower slowly to a full hang before the next rep.
Chin-Up.mistake: Craning the neck to get the chin over the bar instead of pulling the chest up.

steps: Lie under a sturdy bar or table, grip it just wider than your shoulders and hold your body in a straight line.
Pull your chest to the bar by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower under control until your arms are straight, keeping your hips up.
Inverted Row.mistake: Letting the hips sag, which shortens the pull and hides how weak the back is.

steps: Lie face down with your arms extended in front and your legs straight.
Lift your arms, chest and legs a few inches off the floor together, looking at the floor.
Hold for a second, squeezing your glutes and upper back, then lower with control.
Superman.mistake: Cranking the neck upward to look ahead instead of keeping it in line with your spine.

steps: Support yourself on parallel bars with straight arms, shoulders down and chest slightly forward.
Lower until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, elbows tracking back.
Press up until your arms are straight without shrugging your shoulders.
Bodyweight Dip.mistake: Dropping far below parallel with the shoulders rolled forward, which strains the front of the shoulder.

steps: Sit on the edge of a bench, place your hands beside your hips, and slide your hips off with legs out in front.
Bend your elbows straight back and lower until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Press up through your palms until your arms are straight.
Bench Dip.mistake: Sliding too far from the bench and dropping too deep, which overloads the front of the shoulders.

steps: Forearms on the floor with elbows under your shoulders, legs straight, body in one line from head to heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes as if bracing for a punch.
Hold while breathing steadily, keeping your hips level.
Plank.mistake: Letting the lower back sag or the hips rise, which takes the work off the abs.

steps: Lie on your side with your forearm under your shoulder and your legs stacked or staggered.
Lift your hips so your body forms one straight line from head to feet.
Hold, keeping your hips high and your top shoulder stacked over the bottom one.
Side Plank.mistake: Letting the hips drop toward the floor or rolling forward, so the obliques stop working.

steps: On hands and knees with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips, back flat.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are in line with your torso.
Pause for a second without rotating your hips, then return and switch sides.
Bird Dog.mistake: Arching the lower back and letting the hips twist as the leg lifts.

steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, arms by your sides.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top for a second, then lower with control.
Glute Bridge.mistake: Pushing the hips so high that the lower back arches, which shifts the work off the glutes.

steps: Lie on your back with one foot flat on the floor and the other leg extended straight up or out.
Drive through the planted heel to lift your hips until they are level.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly without letting the hips twist.
Single-Leg Glute Bridge.mistake: Dropping one hip as you lift, which turns it into a lower-back arch.

steps: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Drive one knee toward your chest, then switch legs quickly as if running in place.
Keep your hips level and your core tight throughout.
Mountain Climbers.mistake: Bouncing the hips high into the air, which turns the move into a rushed squat thrust.

steps: From standing, squat and place your hands on the floor, then jump or step your feet back to a plank.
Lower your chest to the floor, press back up, and jump or step your feet in under your hips.
Explode up into a jump with your arms overhead, then land softly and go again.
Burpee.mistake: Letting the hips sag in the plank, which loads the lower back instead of the legs and core.

steps: On hands and toes with your knees hovering just off the floor, back flat.
Move opposite hand and foot forward together in small, controlled steps.
Keep your hips low and level and your head in line with your spine.
Bear Crawl.mistake: Pushing the hips up and rocking side to side instead of keeping the back flat.

steps: Lie on your back with your arms overhead and your legs straight, pressing your lower back into the floor.
Lift your shoulders and legs a few inches off the floor, forming a shallow banana shape.
Hold while breathing steadily, keeping your lower back glued to the floor.
Hollow Body Hold.mistake: Letting the lower back lift off the floor, which means the legs are too low for your core strength.

steps: Lie on your back with your arms overhead and your legs straight.
Lift your legs and torso at the same time, reaching your hands toward your toes.
Lower both back down slowly with control, without letting your back arch.
V-Up.mistake: Swinging with momentum so the hip flexors do the work instead of the abs.

steps: Stand on one leg with the other leg extended in front, arms forward for balance.
Sit back and down on the standing leg as low as you can control, keeping the heel flat.
Drive through the heel to stand, keeping the knee tracking over the toes.
Pistol Squat.mistake: Rolling onto the toes or collapsing the knee inward at the bottom.

steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Step forward and lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees, torso upright.
Push through the front foot to return, then switch legs.
Dumbbell Lunge.mistake: Letting the front knee cave inward or the torso lean forward under the load.

steps: Hold one dumbbell upright against your chest with both hands, elbows pointing down.
Sit your hips back and down between your knees until your thighs are at least parallel.
Drive through your whole foot to stand, keeping your chest tall.
Dumbbell Goblet Squat.mistake: Letting the dumbbell pull your chest forward so the lower back rounds.

steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, knees slightly bent.
Push your hips back and slide the dumbbells down your legs with a flat back until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift.mistake: Rounding the lower back or bending the knees too much so it turns into a squat.

steps: Hold the dumbbells at shoulder height with your palms facing forward and your core braced.
Press them straight overhead until your arms are almost straight, close to your ears.
Lower back to shoulder height under control.
Dumbbell Shoulder Press.mistake: Arching the lower back to push the weight up instead of keeping your ribs down.

steps: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms forward, elbows pinned to your sides.
Curl the weights up toward your shoulders without moving your upper arms.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
Dumbbell Bicep Curl.mistake: Swinging the torso to heave the weight up, which takes the work off the biceps.

steps: Hold one dumbbell with both hands overhead, arms straight and elbows close to your ears.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping your upper arms still.
Straighten your arms back to the top, squeezing your triceps.
Dumbbell Tricep Extension.mistake: Letting the elbows flare out to the sides, which shifts the load and strains the elbows.

steps: Hinge at the hips with a flat back and a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down.
Pull the dumbbells toward your hips by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower under control until your arms are straight.
Dumbbell Bent-Over Row.mistake: Standing up as you pull, using body momentum instead of the back muscles.

steps: Lie on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand over your chest, feet flat and shoulder blades pinched.
Lower the dumbbells to the sides of your chest with elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Press them back up until your arms are straight above your chest.
Dumbbell Chest Press.mistake: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides, which stresses the shoulders.

steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and stand facing a sturdy box with one foot fully on top.
Drive through the top foot to stand up tall without pushing off the back foot.
Lower slowly under control, then repeat before switching legs.
Dumbbell Step-Up.mistake: Choosing a box so high that the hips twist and the torso leans to compensate.

steps: Anchor the band at chest height, hold the ends and step back until there is tension, arms straight.
Pull the band toward your ribs by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Return slowly to straight arms without letting the band snap you forward.
Resistance Band Row.mistake: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears instead of pulling them down and back.

steps: Stand on the band with feet shoulder-width apart and hold the ends at your shoulders.
Sit your hips back and down until your thighs are at least parallel.
Drive through your feet to stand against the band's pull.
Resistance Band Squat.mistake: Letting the knees collapse inward as the band tension rises on the way up.

steps: Stand with feet a little wider than shoulder-width, kettlebell on the floor in front of you, and hinge to grip it.
Hike the bell back between your legs, then snap your hips forward to swing it to chest height.
Let it fall back and hinge again, keeping your back flat and the power in your hips.
Kettlebell Swing.mistake: Lifting the bell with the arms and squatting instead of snapping the hips.

steps: Start in a high plank with your hands on two dumbbells and your feet wide for balance.
Row one dumbbell to your ribs while keeping your hips square to the floor.
Lower it under control and repeat on the other side.
Renegade Row.mistake: Twisting the hips open as you row, which wastes the anti-rotation work for the core.

steps: Bar across your upper back, feet shoulder-width apart, chest up and core braced.
Sit back and down until your thighs are at least parallel, knees tracking over your toes.
Drive through your whole foot to stand, keeping your chest up.
Barbell Back Squat.mistake: Letting the hips shoot up first so the lower back rounds and the torso falls forward.

steps: Bar rests on your front shoulders with elbows high, feet shoulder-width apart.
Sit straight down until your thighs are at least parallel, keeping your elbows up.
Drive up through your feet, keeping your torso as upright as you can.
Barbell Front Squat.mistake: Letting the elbows drop, which rolls the bar forward and rounds the upper back.

steps: Eyes under the bar, feet flat, shoulder blades pinched together and down.
Lower the bar to your mid-chest with elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Press up and slightly back over your shoulders until your arms are straight.
Bench Press.mistake: Bouncing the bar off the chest or lifting the hips off the bench.

steps: Lie on an incline bench with your feet flat, shoulder blades pinched and the bar over your upper chest.
Lower the bar to your upper chest with elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Press up until your arms are straight over your shoulders.
Incline Bench Press.mistake: Setting the bench too steep so the shoulders take over from the upper chest.

steps: Bar over mid-foot, hands just outside your legs, back flat and chest up, shoulders over the bar.
Push the floor away and drag the bar up your legs, keeping it close to your body.
Stand tall with hips and knees locked, then lower the bar by sending your hips back.
Deadlift.mistake: Rounding the lower back or jerking the bar off the floor instead of pulling the slack out first.

steps: Stand holding the bar at your thighs with a slight knee bend and a flat back.
Push your hips straight back, sliding the bar down your legs until you feel a deep hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes.
Romanian Deadlift.mistake: Letting the bar drift away from the legs, which loads the lower back.

steps: Grip the bar just outside your shoulders and hold it at your collarbone, elbows slightly in front.
Press the bar straight up, moving your head back and then through as the bar passes your forehead.
Lock out overhead with the bar over your mid-foot, then lower under control.
Overhead Press.mistake: Leaning back and turning it into an incline press instead of squeezing the glutes and bracing the core.

steps: Hinge at the hips with a flat back, bar hanging at arm's length below your shoulders.
Pull the bar to your lower ribs by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower under control without letting your torso rise.
Bent-Over Row.mistake: Standing up a little with each rep so momentum does the pulling.

steps: Sit with your thighs under the pad, grip the bar just wider than your shoulders and lean back slightly.
Pull the bar to your upper chest by driving your elbows down toward your sides.
Let the bar rise under control until your arms are fully stretched.
Lat Pulldown.mistake: Leaning far back and yanking the bar down, which turns the pulldown into a row.

steps: Sit tall with your knees slightly bent, chest up and arms reaching for the handle.
Pull the handle to your lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Return slowly until your arms are straight without rounding your back.
Cable Row.mistake: Rocking the torso back and forth to move the weight instead of keeping it still.

steps: Sit with your back flat against the pad and your feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform.
Lower the platform until your knees are bent about 90 degrees without your hips rolling up.
Press through your whole foot until your legs are almost straight, without locking your knees.
Leg Press.mistake: Going so deep that the lower back lifts off the pad and the pelvis tucks under.

steps: Set the pad just above your heels, lying or sitting snugly in the machine.
Curl your heels toward your glutes by squeezing your hamstrings.
Lower slowly until your legs are almost straight.
Leg Curl Machine.mistake: Lifting the hips off the seat to swing the weight up.

steps: Sit with your back against the pad and the roller just above your ankles.
Extend your legs until they are straight and squeeze your quads at the top.
Lower slowly under control rather than dropping the weight.
Leg Extension Machine.mistake: Kicking the weight up with momentum instead of a smooth, controlled lift.

steps: Adjust the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height, back flat against the pad.
Press the handles overhead until your arms are almost straight.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height without letting the weight stack crash.
Seated Shoulder Press Machine.mistake: Setting the seat too low or high and pressing with the elbows behind the body.
